questions.question: Who is a stranger to contract?
questions.solution_html:
• Stranger to contract: A person who is not a party to the contract and generally
  • cannot sue or be sued on it.
  • Discharge by Performance
  • Performance is the most common mode of discharge of contract. When both parties
  • perform their respective obligations according to the terms of the contract, the contract
  • comes to an end.
  • Performance may be
  • • Actual performance
  • • Attempted or tender performance
  • Actual performance takes place when both parties completely fulfil their promises.
  • Tender performance occurs when one party offers to perform the contract, but the other
  • party refuses to accept it. A valid tender discharge the party from liability.
  • Formation
  • Partnership is formed by agreement between partners. Registration is optional in many

  • A company is formed by registration under the Companies Act and must follow legal

questions.question: Define partnership?
questions.solution_html:
• Partnership: Relationship between persons who agree to share profits of a business
  • carried on by all or any of them acting for all.
  • Discharge by Mutual Agreement
  • A contract is created by mutual consent, and therefore it may also be discharged by
  • mutual agreement of the parties.
  • The important forms are
  • Novation
  • A new contract replaces the old contract either between the same parties or different
  • parties. The old contract is discharged.
  • Alteration
  • The terms of the contract are changed with the consent of all parties.
  • Rescission
  • The parties mutually agree to cancel the contract.
  • Remission
  • The promisee accepts a lesser amount or lesser performance than what was originally
  • agreed.
  • Waiver
  • One party voluntarily gives up his rights under the contract.
  • Legal Status
  • Partnership has no separate legal existence apart from its partners.
  • A company has a separate legal entity distinct from its shareholders.
  • Merchantable Quality
  • When goods are purchased from a dealer by description, the goods must be of
  • merchantable quality. They should be fit for ordinary use and free from hidden defects.
questions.final_answer: merchantable quality. They should be fit for ordinary use and free from hidden defects

questions.question: What is meant by part delivery?
questions.solution_html:
• Part delivery: Delivery of a portion of goods with the intention of delivering the
  • whole.
  • Discharge by Impossibility of Performance
  • Sometimes performance becomes impossible due to circumstances beyond the control of
  • the parties. In such cases, the contract is discharged.
  • Impossibility may be
  • • Initial impossibility
  • • Supervening impossibility
  • Initial impossibility exists at the time of formation of the contract. Supervening
  • impossibility arises after the contract is made.
  • Examples
  • • Destruction of subject matter
  • • Death or incapacity of a party
  • • Change in law
  • • Outbreak of war or natural disaster
  • This is also known as the doctrine of frustration.
  • Liability
  • In partnership, the liability of partners is unlimited. Their personal assets may be used to
  • pay business debts.
  • In a company, shareholders have limited liability.
  • Sale by Description
  • If goods are sold by description, they must correspond exactly with the description
  • provided by the seller.

questions.question: What is right of subrogation?
questions.solution_html:
• Right of subrogation: Right of a surety to step into the shoes of the creditor after
  • paying the debt.
  • Discharge by Operation of Law
  • A contract may be discharged automatically by law in certain situations.
  • Examples
  • • Death of a party in personal contracts
  • • Insolvency
  • • Merger of rights
  • • Material alteration of contract without consent
  • Number of Members
  • Partnership requires a minimum of two persons and has a limited maximum number of
  • partners.
  • A company may have a large number of members, especially in the case of a public
  • company.
  • Sale by Sample
  • When goods are sold by sample, the bulk of goods should correspond with the sample
  • shown. The buyer must also get reasonable opportunity to compare the sample and the
  • goods.

questions.question: Define a contract?
questions.solution_html:
• Contract: An agreement enforceable by law.
  • Discharge by Lapse of Time
  • Every contract must be enforced within the period prescribed by the Limitation Act. If the
  • aggrieved party fails to take action within the specified time, the contract is discharged
  • by lapse of time.
  • Transfer of Interest
  • A partner cannot transfer his interest without the consent of other partners.
  • Shares of a company can generally be transferred easily.
  • Fraud and Misrepresentation
  • The seller cannot escape liability if he makes false statements or intentionally deceives
  • the buyer.
  • Fraud includes deliberate concealment of defects or false representation regarding
  • quality or nature of goods.

questions.question: Differentiate express contract and implied contract?
questions.solution_html:
• Express vs Implied contract
  • o Express: Terms stated clearly (oral/written)
  • o Implied: Inferred from conduct or circumstances
  • Discharge by Breach of Contract
  • When one party fails to perform his obligation, it amounts to breach of contract.
  • Breach may be
  • • Actual breach
  • • Anticipatory breach
  • Actual breach occurs on the due date of performance. Anticipatory breach occurs when
  • one party refuses to perform before the due date.
  • Management
  • Partnership business is managed directly by partners.
  • A company is managed by the Board of Directors elected by shareholders.
  • Active Concealment of Defects
  • If the seller knowingly hides defects from the buyer, the rule of caveat emptor will not
  • apply.

• Discharge of contract means termination of contractual obligations between the parties.

questions.question: What is partnership? Differentiate partnership with accompany.
questions.solution_html:
• According to the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, partnership is the relation between
  • persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any one of
  • them acting for all.
  • Partnership is formed through an agreement between two or more persons to conduct
  • business jointly. The persons are called partners, and collectively they are known as a
  • firm.
  • Features of Partnership
  • • Existence of agreement between partners
  • • Sharing of profits and losses
  • • Mutual agency
  • • Lawful business
  • • Unlimited liability
  • • Utmost good faith among partners
  • • No separate legal entity
  • Difference between Partnership and Company

questions.question: Elaborate exceptions to the general rule “let the buyer beware?
questions.solution_html:
• Elaborate exceptions to the general rule “Let the buyer beware”.
  • The doctrine of “Caveat Emptor” means “Let the buyer beware.” According to this rule
  • the buyer must examine goods carefully before purchasing them. The seller is generally
  • not responsible for defects in goods. However, modern business law recognises several
  • exceptions to protect buyers from unfair practices.
questions.final_answer: exceptions to protect buyers from unfair practices
